title: The Knight's Code
tagline: The greatest knight who ever lived is undone by the greatest love.

scenes.text: Camelot, the age of chivalry. The Knights of the Round Table represent an ideal — not just military skill, but a code of conduct binding warriors to honor, mercy, and service. Lancelot du Lac is the greatest of them — and its most tragic figure.

scenes.speaker: King Arthur
scenes.text: Lancelot, you are the finest knight who ever drew breath. In battle, no man is your equal. In honor — what say you?

scenes.speaker: Lancelot
scenes.text: I serve the code above all men — including kings. And yet... even the finest code meets its limits when the heart is tested. God forgive me.

challenge.fact: Chivalry combined three loyalties: to God (religious duty), to the lord (feudal duty), and to women and the weak (courtly duty). Loyalty to the king was central — a knight who broke this oath was stripped of knighthood.

scenes.text: The medieval chivalric code was not just a literary ideal. Knights were legally bound by oaths of fealty, honor, and protection of the weak. Violation could mean excommunication, exile, or death.

challenge.fact: A knight's training took fourteen years. The progression from page to squire to knight was as formalised as any modern profession. The Round Table's innovation — every seat equal, no place more honoured than another — was a radical reimagining of hierarchy in a world of strict rank.
challenge.instruction: The squires pass notes in a grid code. Read the path every knight must follow.

scenes.speaker: Lancelot
scenes.text: They say the Grail awaits the pure of heart. I have sought it my whole life. But a man cannot unsee what he has done. The quest is not for the Grail — it is for redemption.

challenge.instruction: Medieval troubadours sang of chivalry and courtly love. Arrange the ascending notes of a knightly melody.
challenge.fact: Medieval troubadours spread the code of chivalry through song — their poems and music were the social media of the 12th century, spreading from Provence across all of Europe.

scenes.text: The corridors of Camelot are long and labyrinthine. The true knight who knows the code may navigate them without error...

challenge.fact: Chivalry evolved over three centuries. Early codes (c.1000 CE) emphasised martial courage; by 1200 CE, troubadour poetry had added courtesy and romantic love. By 1300 CE, protection of the poor and weak entered as the Church sought to direct knightly violence toward Christian purposes.

challenge.instruction: Mix the woad blue worn by Frankish knights and medieval dyers — a plant-based indigo that tinted cloth from Celtic Britain to Charlemagne's court.
challenge.fact: Woad (Isatis tinctoria) was Europe's primary source of blue dye for millennia. In the 13th century the woad trade was so valuable it funded Gothic cathedrals in France. It was eventually displaced by imported indigo from India, devastating the European woad industry.

scenes.speaker: Lancelot
scenes.text: Batu Khan waits at Changan, but nothing is happening there, and without an event there is no fight. I will go first; the turn after I arrive, play the Battlefield card on Changan and we attack.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 3 · Starting an Event. Deploy Lancelot to Changan and End Turn. Next turn play the Battlefield card there, add your follower and win one attack.
challenge.fact: Event cards start a scenario at a location where you already have a Great Person, and only one who arrived on an earlier turn can start it. A local event keeps running until a player ends it.
